**Voica v0.7.0 — the vocabulary works without AI, History is readable, and a loud word can no longer kill your recording.**

### New: your vocabulary now works on its own

Until now the term list was a hint for the cloud engine plus an optional AI pass — with the local
engine and the toggle off, it did nothing. Now Voica pulls garbled spellings back to the terms you
listed **by rule**: no API key, no internet, and the same on both engines. Fill in the vocabulary and
it works; the AI toggle stays as an optional pass on top, for what rules cannot do — grammatical case
and badly mangled terms.

The rules match on the consonant skeleton of a word, because vowels are what recognition loses:
`Dпсик`, `Dpсиcк` and `Deepsc` all reduce to the same skeleton as `DeepSeek`. What is required on top
depends on how strong the evidence is — a word written in two alphabets at once is proof of mangling
by itself, plain Latin also has to be close letter by letter, plain Cyrillic only ever matches an
exact skeleton. Compound terms are searched across two words, so both `клодкод` and `Tail scale` land
on the right spelling. When nothing matches, nothing is touched: the thresholds come from running the
rules over a whole real history, and the traps — «Вика» against `Voica`, «Папа» against `API`,
`Greek` against `Groq`, `vice versa` — are frozen as tests.

Fully offline dictation with correct terms is now possible: local engine, AI toggle off, nothing
leaves the machine.

### New: search in History, including what you actually said

`Ctrl+F` or the field above the list. It searches the finished text **and what the engine heard
before the corrections** — you remember saying "клодкод", not `Claude Code`, and a search over the
final text alone would miss your own dictation. Matches are highlighted, and when a record was found
only through that original text, it is shown underneath so you can see what matched.

Side effect worth having: the history becomes a log of what recognition does to your terms — search
one and see every way the engine has ever mangled it.

### Changed: the History window has two panes

The list on the left, the record's text on the right — wrapped, scrollable, selectable. A dictation
longer than a sentence could not be read at all in the old one-line rows. Language, length and engine
now sit in the line under the text. Export is unchanged: it remains an action over the whole history,
not over what the search left on screen.

### Fixed: a loud word could silently kill your recording

The level meter behind the recording capsule computed its peak with `Math.Abs` on a 16-bit sample —
which overflows on exactly the value a microphone produces when the input clips. The exception left
the capture callback and took the capture thread with it, so the app went on "recording" nothing
while you kept talking. One dictation of 5 minutes 48 seconds came back as 40 seconds of text.

Fixed, and the capture path now carries nothing but writing your audio to the file. On top of that, a
microphone that stops sending audio for any reason is noticed within three seconds: the dictation
ends at once, says so, and transcribes what was captured instead of leaving you talking into a dead
microphone.

### Also fixed

- **A phrase could appear twice** in a long dictation on the local engine, where two windows meet.
  They had heard one word differently — «управляющий» against «управляющего» — and that single word
  was enough to lose the overlap, so both copies reached the text.
- **A bare Left Alt hotkey now warns** that Windows switches the keyboard layout with Alt+Shift and
  the layout will stop switching. The key stays on offer — Settings just says so under it.
- Settings explain what the vocabulary does now, and the long hints moved into info dots.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.7.0.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
